title: Marguerite and the Wolf
premise: Wren Winterbourne, a bone-carver who hears the dead, keeps the ledgers of the Guild of Impossible Things — until he finds tonight's date inscribed in a century-old book of prophecies and is pulled bodily into its pages. There he discovers Marguerite, a wolf-bound queen whose memory was stolen to crown a usurper king, and learns the prophecy demands a thirteenth moon: either the true ruler restored or the land devoured. To unbind the king from the thing wearing his crown, Wren must trade his own gift of hearing the dead, carving Marguerite's stolen memories back into her bones. In the end, justice arrives outside any law — the guild's ledgers burn, Marguerite refuses the throne she reclaimed, and Wren returns deaf to ghosts but free, with the prophecy rewritten in his own hand.
about_author: Mara Zhou is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing estate ledgers and swears one of them answered back. She writes fantasy about inheritance, bureaucracy, and the people history forgets to record.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Tonight
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. While balancing the guild's accounts of impossible trades, Wren hears a dead clerk whisper that tonight's date appears in the Prophecy of Thirteen Moons — then the ledger pulls him through its own page. He lands in a moonlit forest where a wolf with human eyes watches him. Emotional beat: disorientation curdling into dread as he realizes the dead have been keeping appointments with him all along.

chapters.title: What the Crown Remembers
chapters.summary: Alternating Wren and Marguerite POVs. The wolf reveals herself as Queen Marguerite, unmade a century ago when the guild traded her memories to crown a hollow king. Wren, able to hear what the dead remember, begins recovering fragments from her bones. Emotional beat: wary alliance deepening into grief, as Marguerite confronts that her own sister brokered the trade.

chapters.title: The Twelfth Turning
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, closing on Wren. With one moon left, they infiltrate the palace where the thing wearing the crown feeds on borrowed memory. The guild offers Wren absolution if he abandons her; instead he steals the original ledger of her sale. Betrayed by a guide, Marguerite is captured, and Wren must choose between his gift and her freedom. Emotional beat: sacrifice — he carves her memories into her bones using his own hearing as payment.

chapters.title: A Hand Unbound
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Restored, Marguerite faces the crowned thing at the thirteenth turning — but refuses both throne and vengeance, unbinding the king from it by naming it truly, outside any law. The guild's ledgers burn; the prophecy ends blank where Wren stands. Deaf to the dead but finally heard himself, he walks out of the book with her. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace after justice no court could grant.
